title: Sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, urosepsis and bacteremia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock only (not the local infection or the organ dysfunction). If none applies, choose 'no code'.
note:
Admission Date: 05/10/2026
Discharge Date: 05/13/2026
Reason for Admission: Fever and malaise.

Hospital Course:
Pt is a 61 y.o. male admitted with fever. Initial labs showed leukocytosis. Blood cultures were drawn and subsequently returned positive for bacteremia. Clinical evaluation and monitoring showed pt remained stable; physician documents that the patient does not have sepsis. Pt tolerated oral intake well. Managed with oral antibiotics during stay. No acute distress noted. Vital signs remained stable throughout admission. Pt cleared for discharge with instructions for home meds.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Bacteremia

Discharge Medications:
Amoxicillin 875mg TID x 10 days
Acetaminophen 650mg PRN for fever

Follow-up:
F/u with PCP in 1 week for wound check and lab review.

Electronically signed,
K. Nguyen, MD
05/13/2026
explanations: Bacteremia without sepsis is coded R78.81 (no HCC), which is not a sepsis code: no sepsis code applies.

distractors.why: The provider documents bacteremia without sepsis.
